source_refs.note: Exercise 12.1, Question 1 (book page 229): limits of four sequences, parts (i)-(iv). Answer key PDF 310 agrees with all four (2, 0, 5/2, 1/2); solution book PDF 1050-1054.

blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find the limit of the following sequences if exists: \(a_n = \frac{2n + 3}{n + 1}\).
blocks.explanation:
Sab se pehle dekhte hain ke sawal kya keh raha hai: yeh sequence (silsila) ka limit hai, yani jab \(n\) barhta hi chala jaye (\(n \to +\infty\)) to \(a_n\) kis number ke qareeb pahunchta hai.
Upar aur neeche dono bohat bare ho jate hain, is liye seedha \(n = \infty\) rakhna \(\infty/\infty\) deta hai, jis ka koi matlab nahi.
Plan: har term ko \(n\) se divide karenge (denominator ki sab se bari power), phir yeh use karenge ke \(1/n\) zero ki taraf jata hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_n = \dfrac{2n + 3}{n + 1}\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\lim\limits_{n \to +\infty} a_n\), agar mojood ho.
Tareeqa: Jab \(n\) ke polynomials ka quotient (taqseem) ho to upar aur neeche dono ko denominator mein \(n\) ki sab se bari power (yahan \(n\)) se divide karte hain. Is ke baad har \(c/n\) wali term zero ki taraf jati hai (12.2.5). Yeh book ka "Methods for Evaluating the Limits at Infinity" wala tareeqa hai.

Pehle samajh lein ke seedha value kyun nahi rakh sakte
\[n = 1000:\ \frac{2003}{1001}\]
Kyun: \(n\) barhne se upar bhi bara aur neeche bhi bara. "Bohat bara taqseem bohat bara" (\(\infty/\infty\)) ka jawab pehle se tay nahi hota: kabhi 2, kabhi 0, kabhi kuch aur. Is liye fraction ki shakal badalni parti hai.

Upar aur neeche ko \(n\) se divide karein
\[a_n = \frac{\dfrac{2n}{n} + \dfrac{3}{n}}{\dfrac{n}{n} + \dfrac{1}{n}}\]
\[= \frac{2 + \dfrac{3}{n}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{n}}\]
Kyun: Kisi fraction ke upar aur neeche ko ek hi non-zero number se divide karne se us ki value nahi badalti, jaise \(6/8 = 3/4\). Faida yeh hua ke ab barhne wali terms ya to constant (2 aur 1) ban gayin ya \(c/n\) jaisi choti terms.

Ab \(n \to +\infty\) karein
\[\lim_{n \to +\infty} a_n = \frac{2 + 0}{1 + 0}\]
\[= 2\]
Kyun: Ek fixed number ko barhte hue \(n\) se divide karo to jawab chhota hota jata hai: \(3/10 = 0.3\), \(3/1000 = 0.003\)... is liye \(3/n \to 0\) aur \(1/n \to 0\). Neeche \(1\) bacha jo zero nahi, is liye quotient theorem lag sakta hai.
Dhyan dein: \(n\) ko kat kar \(2n/n\) ko \(2\) likhna theek hai, lekin \(3\) ko \(n\) se divide karna mat bhooliye; har term ko divide karna zaroori hai.

Tasdeeq
\[a_{1000} = \frac{2003}{1001} \approx 2.001\]
Kyun: Bari value \(n = 1000\) par term \(2\) ke bilkul qareeb hai, jaisa hamara jawab keh raha hai. Is liye sequence converge karti hai (ek number par ja kar tik jati hai).
blocks.final_answer: \(\lim\limits_{n \to +\infty} a_n = 2\) (sequence \(2\) ki taraf converge karti hai).

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Find the limit of the following sequences if exists: \(b_n = \frac{2n + 3}{n^2 + 1}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi sequence ka limit hai, \(n \to +\infty\).
Ghaur karein: neeche \(n^2\) hai aur upar sirf \(n\). Yani denominator numerator se kahin zyada tezi se barhta hai.
Plan: har term ko \(n^2\) se divide karenge, phir \(n \to +\infty\) karenge. Andaza pehle hi laga lein: jab neeche wala zyada tez barhe to fraction zero ki taraf jata hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(b_n = \dfrac{2n + 3}{n^2 + 1}\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\lim\limits_{n \to +\infty} b_n\), agar mojood ho.
Tareeqa: Upar aur neeche ko \(n^2\) se divide karenge, kyunke denominator mein \(n\) ki sab se bari power \(n^2\) hai. Phir \(c/n \to 0\) aur \(c/n^2 \to 0\) use karenge.

Upar aur neeche ko \(n^2\) se divide karein
\[b_n = \frac{\dfrac{2n}{n^2} + \dfrac{3}{n^2}}{\dfrac{n^2}{n^2} + \dfrac{1}{n^2}}\]
\[= \frac{\dfrac{2}{n} + \dfrac{3}{n^2}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{n^2}}\]
Kyun: Denominator ki sab se bari power se divide karne ka faida yeh hai ke neeche ek non-zero number (yahan \(1\)) bach jata hai. Agar hum sirf \(n\) se divide karte to neeche \(n + 1/n\) bachta jo phir bhi barhta rehta, aur kaam adhoora reh jata.
Dhyan dein: \(2n/n^2 = 2/n\) hai, \(2\) nahi. Power ghatate waqt dhyan rakhein.

Ab \(n \to +\infty\) karein
\[\lim_{n \to +\infty} b_n = \frac{0 + 0}{1 + 0}\]
\[= 0\]
Kyun: \(2/n\), \(3/n^2\) aur \(1/n^2\) teenon zero ki taraf jate hain. Upar \(0\) aur neeche \(1\), aur \(0 \div 1 = 0\). Yeh \(0/0\) wali mushkil nahi, kyunke neeche \(1\) hai, zero nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[b_{1000} = \frac{2003}{1000001} \approx 0.002\]
Kyun: Bari \(n\) par term bohat chhoti hai, zero ke qareeb. Sequence zero par converge karti hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(\lim\limits_{n \to +\infty} b_n = 0\) (sequence \(0\) ki taraf converge karti hai).

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Find the limit of the following sequences if exists: \(c_n = \frac{5n}{2n + 3}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi sequence ka limit hai, \(n \to +\infty\). Upar aur neeche dono mein \(n\) ki power 1 hai (degree barabar).
Seedha rakhne se \(\infty/\infty\) milta hai, jo undecided (ghair waazeh) hai.
Plan: \(n\) se divide karenge, phir \(n \to +\infty\). Andaza: degree barabar ho to jawab leading coefficients (sab se bari power ke saath wale numbers) ki nisbat hota hai, yani \(5/2\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(c_n = \dfrac{5n}{2n + 3}\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\lim\limits_{n \to +\infty} c_n\), agar mojood ho.
Tareeqa: Upar aur neeche ko \(n\) se divide karenge (denominator ki sab se bari power), phir \(3/n \to 0\) use karenge.

Upar aur neeche ko \(n\) se divide karein
\[c_n = \frac{\dfrac{5n}{n}}{\dfrac{2n}{n} + \dfrac{3}{n}}\]
\[= \frac{5}{2 + \dfrac{3}{n}}\]
Kyun: Fraction ki value wohi rehti hai, lekin ab barhne wali terms constant ban gayin: \(5n/n = 5\) aur \(2n/n = 2\). Sirf \(3/n\) bachi jo chhoti hoti jati hai.

Ab \(n \to +\infty\) karein
\[\lim_{n \to +\infty} c_n = \frac{5}{2 + 0}\]
\[= \frac{5}{2}\]
Kyun: \(3/n \to 0\), neeche \(2\) bacha jo zero nahi, is liye quotient theorem lagta hai.
Dhyan dein: Kuch students \(5n/(2n+3)\) mein \(n\) "kaat" kar \(5/(2+3)\) likh dete hain. Yeh ghalat hai; \(n\) sirf \(2n\) mein factor hai, \(3\) mein nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[c_{1000} = \frac{5000}{2003} \approx 2.496\]
Kyun: Yeh \(5/2 = 2.5\) ke bohat qareeb hai, is liye jawab sahi hai aur sequence converge karti hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Find the limit of the following sequences if exists: \(d_n = \frac{n^2 - 3n + 1}{2n^2 + n + 4}\).
blocks.explanation:
Sequence ka limit, \(n \to +\infty\). Upar aur neeche dono ki degree 2 hai.
Seedha rakhne se phir \(\infty/\infty\) aata hai.
Plan: har term ko \(n^2\) se divide karenge, phir \(n \to +\infty\). Andaza: degree barabar hai, to jawab \(n^2\) ke coefficients ki nisbat \(1/2\) hona chahiye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(d_n = \dfrac{n^2 - 3n + 1}{2n^2 + n + 4}\).
Humein find karna hai: \(\lim\limits_{n \to +\infty} d_n\), agar mojood ho.
Tareeqa: Upar aur neeche ko \(n^2\) se divide karenge (denominator ki sab se bari power). Phir har \(c/n\) aur \(c/n^2\) zero ki taraf jayegi.

Upar aur neeche ko \(n^2\) se divide karein
\[d_n = \frac{1 - \dfrac{3}{n} + \dfrac{1}{n^2}}{2 + \dfrac{1}{n} + \dfrac{4}{n^2}}\]
Kyun: Ek ek term ko alag divide kiya: \(n^2/n^2 = 1\), \(3n/n^2 = 3/n\), \(1/n^2\) waisi hi; neeche \(2n^2/n^2 = 2\), \(n/n^2 = 1/n\), aur \(4/n^2\). Teen terms upar aur teen neeche, koi term chhootni nahi chahiye.

Ab \(n \to +\infty\) karein
\[\lim_{n \to +\infty} d_n = \frac{1 - 0 + 0}{2 + 0 + 0}\]
\[= \frac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: Jis term ke neeche \(n\) ya \(n^2\) hai woh bari \(n\) par zero ke qareeb ho jati hai. Neeche \(2\) bacha jo zero nahi.
Dhyan dein: \(-3/n\) ka minus sign zero ban jane par koi farq nahi dalta, lekin isay likhna na bhoolein; exam mein har term dikhana zaroori hai.

Tasdeeq
\[d_{1000} = \frac{997001}{2001004} \approx 0.498\]
Kyun: Yeh \(1/2 = 0.5\) ke qareeb hai. Is se pakka ho gaya ke sequence \(1/2\) par converge karti hai.
